finding.claim: Authorization bypass in the ban endpoint. require_admin() calls abort(403), which raises werkzeug HTTPException (a subclass of Exception). The ban() handler wraps the call in try/except Exception and only logs a warning, so execution falls through to do_ban(uid) for non-admin users.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST; uid is attacker-controlled
require_admin(g.user) is called for non-admin user
Only logs a warning; no return or re-raise

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only control and is neutralised by the broad except. The unban route (line 26) calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is correctly enforced. No other middleware or before_request checks exist in the file. Secondary issue: the log line at 19 writes a user-supplied name, which may allow log injection.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at admin.py:9-11 (aborts with 403 via exception). It is neutralised by the broad `except Exception` at admin.py:18-19, which logs and falls through. No before_request or other middleware exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20, abort(403) from require_admin (line 11) is an HTTPException caught by `except Exception` (line 18), which only logs, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for non-admin users; unban (line 26) is unguarded by try/except and so is correctly enforced.
